public_rationale: A documented counterexample defeats the claim that nobody had succeeded. In June 2023, the vLLM developers reported that LMSYS could serve its LLM traffic with 50% fewer GPUs. This concerns computing resources, not merely lower API prices.
limitations: The deployment result is reported by the developers.
It does not establish that every model became more efficient or that any provider became profitable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nobody has succeeded in making LLMs more efficient.

statement.excerpt: Nobody is trying to make these things more efficient, or at the very least nobody has succeeded in doing so.

from_speaker: at the very least nobody has succeeded
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that no one had demonstrated greater efficiency in operating LLMs by publication.
Efficiency means using fewer computing resources for comparable model outputs and workloads. A lower retail price alone is insufficient.

The surrounding discussion starts in November 2022. I use that month through publication as the observation period; this is a cumulative claim about achievements, not a quarterly financial observation.
criteria.support_condition: Credible, sufficiently comprehensive evidence establishes that no demonstrated LLM efficiency improvement existed during the period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one documented implementation performs comparable LLM work with fewer computing resources during the period.
